title: Vega OS: Screen and controls
lead: Use the Vega app with a remote to load a source, edit playback settings, inspect applied code and compare SDK results and events. Its native screen differs from the browser UI and the Android-based Fire TV app.

blocks.text: The video occupies the upper part of the screen; the controls and editors scroll below it. Use D-pad and Select on a device, or arrow keys and Enter on a Vega Virtual Device. Buttons and focusable switches operate the app. There is no browser Player control bar or shared HTML theme picker on this screen.

blocks.title: Before opening the screen
blocks.text: Use the Kepler build for Vega OS, not the Android Fire TV package. The Player app identifier is com.playerlab.vega and the component is com.playerlab.vega.main. Generate the local runtime configuration and rebuild when licenses change. Follow the linked setup and Vega README for the supported SDK profile, build and device-selection commands.

items.label: Build and launch the Kepler app
Implementation guide: native media, settings and UI changes

blocks.text: Choose a source and apply a change

blocks.caption: The configuration form below the native video. This view shows external subtitle fields, a start offset and the Autoplay/Mute switches; the form continues below the capture.

items: Select a VOD preset and confirm that video frames and the position advance. VOD means on-demand media with a fixed timeline. Autoplay and Mute on startup are initially enabled; if Autoplay is off, use PlayerAPI.play in SDK API experiments.

Open Show configuration and record the current values. Enter an HTTP/HTTPS source URL and choose its actual HLS, DASH or progressive MP4 type. HLS and DASH can provide multiple qualities. Optional title and poster values are stored with the source; this native screen does not draw poster artwork.

For an initial-position comparison, keep the source URL, enter 5 in Start offset (seconds), choose Start and select Apply and recreate player. After the source loads, compare the position and picture with the original playback.

Apply validates the whole draft, waits for the old native session to close and recreates the Player. A source-only form edit also restarts playback from its configured offset. Invalid or unchanged values do not replace the session.

Reset draft discards unapplied edits. To undo an applied experiment, restore the recorded values and Apply. To restore the initial Player inputs, enable Autoplay and Mute on startup and clear both buffer fields and Maximum video bitrate. A VOD preset restores its source fields, not all Player settings.

rows: Compare the starting position after Apply. Start uses the beginning of the media/live window; End uses the end/live edge. SDK default is Start for VOD and End for live. Signed offsets are accepted.
Compare the new session after Apply. If automatic playback is disabled, use the SDK API play command. A startup flag is not an immediate pause or unmute command.

Compare buffer.video.forwardduration and buffer.audio.forwardduration in applied code. Positive values set media buffer targets; blank restores SDK defaults. This does not extend the live rewind window.
Compare adaptation.bitrates.maxSelectableVideoBitrate, the selected quality and playback on a source with several qualities. Blank removes the cap; enter the value without units or commas.

blocks.text: The form accepts finite decimal offsets and positive buffer/bitrate targets. The native media integration requires Fetch; choosing XHR in advanced configuration is rejected before Apply. Additional type-level choices do not create missing browser capabilities. See the implementation guide for the configuration paths and platform conditions.

blocks.caption: A plain WebVTT cue displayed over the native video. The settings below it remain usable; this is an app-rendered text overlay rather than the browser subtitle UI.

items: Keep Autoplay enabled for a basic playback comparison, or use PlayerAPI.play and PlayerAPI.pause in SDK API experiments. On live media with a rewind window, compare Live edge and the available rewind buttons with the position/state line. Allow DVR controls the app’s rewind helper.

For an external subtitle, enter a reachable HTTPS WebVTT URL, Subtitle label and Subtitle language together. WebVTT contains timed subtitle cues; use a file aligned with the selected media. A language tag such as en-US identifies the language.

Enable external subtitle on load and Apply. Play through the cue times and check the text over the picture. This switch enables the track on load; unlike React Native’s Mark as default metadata field, it does not require selecting a browser subtitle menu.

To remove the external subtitle, clear its URL and Apply. The label/language are cleared with it. Reset draft only cancels pending edits; it does not remove an already applied track. The native text display renders plain cue text rather than HTML subtitle styling.

blocks.title: Returning to the app
blocks.text: Returning from the background creates a new session from the retained source and applied settings, using its start offset and Autoplay choice. It does not restore an arbitrary previous position. If the app reports that native media release is unconfirmed, restart the app before trying again; repeated Apply cannot confirm that the old media resources were released.

blocks.caption: Show applied code in the Vega app. Code lines can receive remote focus so the ScrollView reveals lines below the video. License values use placeholders.

items: After Apply, open Show applied code. Compare the source and Player settings with the recorded baseline. The output contains applied values and approved callback bodies, not pending draft edits.
Use D-pad Down/Up to read the output. Each line participates in focus and scrolling. This TV app has no clipboard integration; it does not provide React Native’s Copy code action.
Edit a value without applying and confirm that the output still represents the active configuration. Reset draft cancels that edit. To undo an applied value, restore the previous value and Apply.

For integration details, follow the implementation guide. Reusing the displayed configuration still requires the existing native media initialization, surface connection and release sequence; the output is not a standalone browser player.

items.label: How configuration connects to native media and UI

blocks.caption: The typed configuration editor shows a callback signature, body and explicit permission control. Apply installs the approved callback before the matching request is tried.

items: Open Show configuration and Show all SDK configuration. Search an exact PlayerConfig or SourceConfig path and select Set Vega API value. The SDK is the Player library; its API defines the available configuration, commands and events.

Use the displayed type to enter scalar values, enumeration choices, object fields, dictionaries, lists or bytes. Add array items in order and fill required related fields. Keep the previous value or whether an override was absent.

For a function, enter its JavaScript body, read its argument/return contract and enable Allow this SDK callback. Apply installs the function; it runs when the SDK invokes it. A JavaScript value factory for an any-typed value can run during Apply or Run.

After Apply, compare Show applied code and the relevant result or event. Remove the override and Apply to restore the basic form value or SDK default. Removing a callback stops future calls after replacement; restore any Player state that the callback deliberately changed.

blocks.text: Edited JavaScript runs inside the app without a sandbox, so enable only code you trust. Binary inputs accept hexadecimal or Base64 and become buffers or typed arrays; entering a DRM certificate does not supply compatible content, a license service or device support. The implementation guide explains configuration types and native limitations.
Run commands and inspect state and events

blocks.caption: PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime during playback. The result appears below Run Vega SDK API; the picture and SDK events provide additional context.

items: Open Show SDK API experiments, search PlayerAPI.getCurrentTime and choose a call signature if needed. Optional arguments can be supplied or omitted. Select Run Vega SDK API and read the call and its value or error.

Run the time query again while media advances, and compare seconds with the picture. Inspect current SDK API availability only checks whether methods exist; it does not call them or demonstrate their feature behavior.

To compare a command, read PlayerAPI.getVolume, record its value, run PlayerAPI.setVolume and read it again. Restore the recorded volume afterward. A returned value, a setter or an empty result should be checked against the relevant state/events.

Use SDK events, Pause Vega event log and Clear Vega event log to isolate the relevant notifications. For on/off experiments, remove the same callback instance that was registered. Query any required SDK objects from the current session after recreation.

Use Recreate Vega player after destroying the Player or to return to the applied configuration. The replacement waits for the previous media session to release. It does not undo saved source/configuration changes; restore those in the form when needed.

blocks.caption: The SDK returned volume 17 after a callback changed it in this captured experiment. Compare a setter with the getter, then restore the value recorded before your own test.

blocks.text: Manifest methods depend on the loaded format: HLS track helpers need HLS, while DASH period helpers need DASH. Low-latency controls need an appropriate live source; on VOD a target may be accepted while latency remains zero. Match the content and native capabilities to the feature instead of treating every callable Web API as active on Vega.

items: Use an HLS source containing insertion markers; the Vega README links a public sample. In Show all SDK configuration, select PlayerConfig.tweaks.enable_sgai_handling, choose true and Apply.
In SDK API experiments, inspect PlayerAPI.sgai.list for the schedule. PlayerAPI.sgai.getActiveAd reports the active inserted content and is normally empty outside an insertion interval.

While an applicable insertion is active, try PlayerAPI.sgai.skip and compare AdStarted, AdSkipped, AdBreakFinished and subsequent playback. A scheduled insertion alone does not show that the content was reached.
To end the experiment, restore the previous source and remove the SGAI override if it was added, then Apply. Compare the loaded source and applied code with the recorded baseline.

blocks.text: SGAI means server-guided ad insertion: playback follows HLS insertion markers rather than a client-side ad integration. If the scheduled position is outside the media window, compare the stream’s program date time with the insertion start. The browser HTML UI and client-side advertising are not supplied by this native host. See the implementation guide and official Vega limitations for feature prerequisites.
